title: LabVantage vs SampleManager: Which LIMS Platform Is Better for Modern Laboratories?
summary: Compare LabVantage vs SampleManager across LIMS, ELN, SDMS, compliance, workflow automation, analytics, and scalability to find the best laboratory platform.
body_markdown:
## **TL;DR**


- LabVantage and Thermo Fisher SampleManager are two of the most established enterprise LIMS platforms used in regulated laboratory environments.
- Both provide LIMS, ELN, SDMS, workflow automation, compliance controls, and instrument integrations.
- LabVantage emphasizes configurability, no-code workflows, and a unified informatics platform for multiple industries.
- SampleManager is widely adopted in QA/QC, manufacturing, and process-driven laboratories with strong compliance and enterprise integration capabilities.


Organizations evaluating **LabVantage vs SampleManager** are typically searching for a laboratory informatics platform capable of supporting complex workflows, regulatory compliance, sample management, and enterprise-scale operations.


Both platforms have decades of adoption across pharmaceutical, biotech, manufacturing, environmental, food and beverage, and quality control laboratories. However, their strengths, implementation approaches, and user experiences differ significantly.

## **LabVantage vs SampleManager at a Glance**


### **What Is LabVantage?**


[LabVantage](https://www.scispot.com/blog/labvantage-review) is an enterprise laboratory informatics platform that combines:


- LIMS
- ELN
- [SDMS](https://www.scispot.com/sdms)
- LES
- Workflow automation
- Analytics
- Instrument integrations


The platform is known for its flexibility, configurability, and industry-specific accelerators that help laboratories manage sample lifecycles, testing workflows, quality processes, and compliance requirements.


### **What Is SampleManager?**


Thermo Fisher Scientific's[SampleManager](https://www.scispot.com/blog/samplemanager-review) is a comprehensive laboratory informatics platform designed for laboratory operations, quality management, process development, and manufacturing support.


The platform includes:


- [LIMS](https://www.scispot.com/lims)
- [ELN](https://www.scispot.com/elns)
- SDMS
- LES
- Workflow automation
- Enterprise integrations
- Analytics and AI capabilities


SampleManager is widely used across pharmaceutical, manufacturing, environmental, energy, and testing laboratories.

## **Feature Comparison: LabVantage vs SampleManager**


### **LIMS and Sample Management**


Both platforms provide comprehensive sample lifecycle management.


LabVantage supports sample registration, testing workflows, inventory management, environmental monitoring, stability studies, barcode tracking, and[advanced workflow automation](https://www.scispot.com/workflow-automation) .


SampleManager provides extensive sample tracking, chain-of-custody support, testing workflows, laboratory execution management, and compliance-focused operational controls.


Organizations seeking modern sample management solutions may also explore Scispot's[laboratory management platform.](https://www.scispot.com/lims)


### **ELN, SDMS, and Laboratory Execution**


One of the biggest similarities between the platforms is their integrated approach.


LabVantage combines ELN, LES, and SDMS within a unified environment to support laboratory workflows and scientific documentation.


SampleManager similarly integrates ELN, SDMS, and LES capabilities to help laboratories centralize scientific records, procedural execution, and operational data.


### **Workflow Automation and Configuration**


Workflow flexibility is often a deciding factor during software selection.


LabVantage is recognized for its highly configurable architecture, workflow designer, no-code configuration options, and industry-specific templates. Laboratories can tailor workflows without extensive custom development.


SampleManager focuses heavily on process standardization, automated laboratory execution, SOP-driven workflows, and quality-focused operations.

### **Compliance and Regulatory Support**


Compliance remains a critical requirement for enterprise laboratories.


LabVantage supports regulatory requirements including:


- FDA requirements
- ISO 17025
- HIPAA
- GDPR
- CLIA
- GAMP guidelines


The platform includes electronic signatures, audit trails, security controls, and compliance reporting.


SampleManager supports:


- GMP environments
- [ISO 17025](https://www.scispot.com/blog/iso-17025-compliance-guide-requirements-software-best-practices)
- FDA 21 CFR Part 11
- ALCOA++ principles
- Quality management processes


It is widely used in highly regulated QA/QC environments.


### **Analytics and AI Capabilities**


Laboratories increasingly expect informatics platforms to deliver operational intelligence.


LabVantage provides dashboards, advanced analytics, reporting tools, and workflow visibility features.


SampleManager has expanded its analytics capabilities with business intelligence dashboards, predictive analytics, forecasting, anomaly detection, and AI-assisted workflows.

## **LabVantage vs SampleManager for Different Types of Labs**


### **Pharmaceutical and Biotech Laboratories**


Both platforms have strong adoption in pharmaceutical and biotechnology environments.


LabVantage is often selected by organizations seeking configurable workflows and broad scientific informatics capabilities.


SampleManager is commonly evaluated by organizations focused on QA/QC operations, manufacturing support, and regulated testing environments.


### **Manufacturing and Quality Control Laboratories**


SampleManager has historically maintained a strong presence in manufacturing quality laboratories because of its process execution, compliance, and quality management capabilities.


### **Environmental and Testing Laboratories**


Both platforms support environmental, food testing, petrochemical, and contract laboratory environments through configurable workflows and compliance support.


### **Enterprise Laboratory Networks**


Organizations managing multiple sites often evaluate:


- Scalability
- Deployment flexibility
- Workflow standardization
- Integration capabilities
- Governance controls


Both platforms support enterprise-scale deployments, although implementation approaches may differ.
